bottleneck: Approved gene therapies cost hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars per patient — Zolgensma and Luxturna are landmark examples — reflecting development costs spread over tiny populations and complex manufacturing. Health systems cannot absorb these prices at scale, and most of the world's patients are excluded entirely, creating a two-tier medicine divided by wealth. The pricing model that sustains development simultaneously rations access, and no alternative model has proven viable at scale.
current_state: Outcomes-based contracts and installment plans are experiments, not solutions. Affordability remains the central unresolved question of the gene therapy era, with access concentrated in wealthy countries.

title: Million-dollar pricing rations gene therapy access
why_it_blocks: A cure affordable only to the wealthy is a scientific triumph and a public-health failure. Until pricing and manufacturing allow scale, gene therapy's benefits accrue to a fraction of patients while the rest watch.
